title: ZBiotics vs Cheers Restore: Which Hangover Product Is Worth It?
excerpt: ZBiotics vs Cheers Restore, compared honestly: how the probiotic drink and the DHM capsule work, when to take each, cost per night out, and what the evidence shows.
metaDescription: ZBiotics vs Cheers Restore compared: how the probiotic drink and DHM capsules work, when to take each, cost per night out, and what the evidence really shows.
author: DHM Guide Team
content:
**The honest answer first:** ZBiotics and Cheers Restore go after hangovers in completely different ways, and neither has strong independent human evidence behind it. ZBiotics is a probiotic drink made with bacteria engineered to break down acetaldehyde (a toxic by-product of alcohol) in your gut. Cheers Restore is a capsule built around DHM (dihydromyricetin), a plant compound studied for how it affects alcohol in the body and brain. If you want one bottle you drink before going out and you don't mind paying a lot per night, ZBiotics is the simpler routine. If you'd rather take a pill and want the ingredient with more published research behind it, Cheers is the better fit. And if price matters, plain DHM from another brand gets you the main ingredient in Cheers for a fraction of the cost.

**The quick comparison:** ZBiotics usually costs well over ten dollars a night. Cheers runs about three dollars a serving at the price we last tracked. Pure DHM can be under a dollar. Both brands are premium-priced for what they contain, and neither one replaces drinking less, eating, and drinking water.

> **This is not medical advice.** This article compares two consumer products using published research and the companies' own descriptions. It is not a substitute for a doctor or pharmacist who knows your health history. Neither product is approved by the FDA to prevent or treat hangovers, and neither makes it safe to drive or to drink more. **Ask a doctor or pharmacist first if** you take prescription medicine, are pregnant or breastfeeding, have liver disease, or have a weakened immune system. If someone shows signs of alcohol poisoning, such as confusion, vomiting while drowsy, slow or irregular breathing, or can't be woken up, call 911.

We don't have an affiliate relationship with ZBiotics or Cheers, so you'll find plain links to their websites below. We do earn a commission on some of the DHM products mentioned near the end, and we say so where they appear.

## ZBiotics vs Cheers at a Glance

| | ZBiotics Pre-Alcohol Probiotic | Cheers Restore |
|---|---|---|
| Format | Small single-serve drink | Capsules |
| Main ingredient | Engineered *Bacillus subtilis* probiotic | DHM plus supporting ingredients |
| What it targets | Acetaldehyde made in the gut | Alcohol's effects on the brain and liver |
| When you take it | Before your first drink | Around drinking, per the label |
| Typical cost per night | Roughly $10 to $15 | About $3 per serving, more on heavy nights |
| Independent human evidence | Very limited | Limited (more animal research on DHM) |
| Who makes it | ZBiotics Company | Cheers Health |
| Official site | [zbiotics.com](https://zbiotics.com) | [cheershealth.com](https://cheershealth.com) |

Prices change often and depend on pack size and subscriptions, so treat those numbers as a rough guide and check each company's current pricing.

## How ZBiotics Works: A Probiotic Built to Break Down Acetaldehyde

When you drink, your body breaks alcohol down in two main steps. First, it turns alcohol (ethanol) into **acetaldehyde**, a toxic compound linked to nausea, flushing, and a pounding heart. Then it turns acetaldehyde into acetate, which is mostly harmless. Your liver does the large majority of this work, using enzymes called alcohol dehydrogenase and aldehyde dehydrogenase.

ZBiotics takes a different angle. Its makers took a common probiotic bacterium, *Bacillus subtilis*, and genetically engineered it to produce aldehyde dehydrogenase, the enzyme that breaks acetaldehyde down. The idea is that some alcohol gets turned into acetaldehyde in your digestive tract, partly by the bacteria already living there, and the engineered probiotic can break some of that down before it causes trouble.

A few things are worth knowing about how it's meant to be used:

- **It's a drink, taken before alcohol.** You drink one bottle before your first alcoholic drink. The company's guidance is built around that timing.
- **It doesn't lower your blood alcohol.** ZBiotics is clear on this point itself: it doesn't make you less drunk and doesn't affect how fast your blood alcohol drops. It's not a way to sober up or to drive.
- **It's a probiotic, not a drug.** It's sold as a food product, which means it hasn't gone through the drug approval process and can't legally claim to prevent or treat a hangover.

### The honest limits of the ZBiotics idea

The concept is clever, and lab work shows the engineered strain does produce the enzyme and break down acetaldehyde. The open questions are about how much that matters in a real person:

- **Most acetaldehyde is made in the liver, not the gut.** The gut does produce some, but the liver handles most alcohol. How much of the acetaldehyde that affects how you feel the next day starts in the gut is not well established.
- **Acetaldehyde's role in hangovers is debated.** Hangovers usually peak when blood alcohol is already near zero, and some hangover researchers think inflammation, poor sleep, and dehydration explain more of the next-day misery than acetaldehyde does.
- **Independent human trials are thin.** The company has shared results from its own testing, but as of this writing we haven't found a large, independent, peer-reviewed human trial showing that ZBiotics reduces hangover symptoms.

None of that means it doesn't work for anyone. Plenty of customers report feeling better, and the mechanism is plausible. It means the evidence is closer to "interesting idea with company-backed data" than "proven in independent trials."

## How Cheers Restore Works: A DHM-Based Formula

Cheers Restore is a capsule supplement from Cheers Health. Its main ingredient is **DHM (dihydromyricetin)**, a flavonoid found in the Japanese raisin tree (*Hovenia dulcis*), which has a long history in traditional medicine in East Asia for alcohol-related complaints. The formula also includes supporting ingredients; versions have included things like L-cysteine, milk thistle, and B vitamins. Formulas change, so check the current label for exact amounts.

DHM is thought to work in two main ways:

1. **In the brain.** Alcohol acts on GABA-A receptors, the same calming receptors targeted by some anti-anxiety drugs. A 2012 rat study published in the *Journal of Neuroscience* found DHM blunted alcohol's effects on these receptors and reduced signs of intoxication and withdrawal in the animals.
2. **In the liver.** Later mouse studies from the same research group suggested DHM may help the liver process alcohol and acetaldehyde more efficiently and may protect liver cells from some alcohol-related stress.

### The honest limits of the Cheers idea

DHM has more published research behind it than ZBiotics' engineered strain, but most of it is in animals and cells. Human trials are small, and many test DHM-containing extracts or multi-ingredient products rather than DHM alone. We don't know of a large independent trial of Cheers Restore itself.

The supporting ingredients add less than the label suggests. L-cysteine and milk thistle have some research for liver support in other contexts, and B vitamins are cheap and generally harmless, but none of them has strong evidence for hangovers specifically.

The other practical issue is dose. How much DHM you get per serving, and how many capsules a serving takes, depends on the current formula. Check the label rather than assuming, and compare the DHM amount to what you'd get from a pure DHM product.

## Which Has Better Evidence?

Neither product is strongly proven in people, so this is a comparison between two incomplete pictures:

- **ZBiotics** rests on a solid lab mechanism (the engineered bacteria really do make the enzyme), an unproven assumption (that gut acetaldehyde matters much for hangovers), and limited human data that comes mostly from the company.
- **Cheers Restore** rests on DHM, which has a larger body of independent research, including several animal studies from university labs, but still only small and limited human trials.

If you weigh independent research most heavily, DHM is ahead. It's not a big lead, and it's a lead for the ingredient, not for the Cheers brand specifically. Any good DHM product would share it.

Be skeptical of any marketing, from either company or from anyone else, that promises you'll wake up feeling fine no matter how much you drink. The research doesn't support that for any hangover product.

## Timing: When to Take Each One

Timing is where the two products differ most in daily use.

**ZBiotics: before your first drink.** The whole design relies on the probiotic being in your gut when alcohol arrives. If you forget and remember halfway through the night, the company's own guidance suggests you've missed the best window. It also only covers one night per bottle.

**Cheers Restore: around drinking, by the label.** Cheers' directions tie the serving to how much you drink. DHM-based products are generally taken before or during drinking, and some people take more at the end of the night. That's more flexible than ZBiotics if you forget to plan ahead, but you're swallowing several capsules rather than one small drink.

Whichever you choose, the habits that matter most don't change: eat before you drink, pace yourself, and alternate with water. Our [how to prevent a hangover](/never-hungover/how-to-prevent-a-hangover) guide covers those with the evidence behind each.

## Price per Night Out: Both Are Premium

This is the part both brands would rather you didn't calculate.

- **ZBiotics:** one bottle per night of drinking. At the prices we've seen, that's roughly $10 to $15 a night, with bulk packs and subscriptions at the lower end. For someone who goes out twice a week, that's well over $1,000 a year.
- **Cheers Restore:** about $3 per serving at the price we last tracked. Heavier nights can call for more than one serving, which pushes it toward $6 or more.
- **Pure DHM from other brands:** often under $1 per serving. [Double Wood DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20), for example, has 1,000 mg of DHM per serving at about $0.80 at the price we last tracked (affiliate link).

So the honest price ranking is: ZBiotics costs the most per night by a wide margin, Cheers is in the middle, and plain DHM is cheapest. Part of what you pay for with both ZBiotics and Cheers is branding, convenience, and packaging.

## Can You Take ZBiotics and Cheers Together?

There's no known reason they'd conflict. They work in different places: ZBiotics in the gut, DHM mainly in the liver and brain. But nobody has studied the combination, so there's no evidence that stacking them works better than either one alone. You'd also be paying for both, which makes an already expensive night more expensive.

If you're curious, a cheaper experiment is to try each one on its own on a couple of similar nights (same drinks, same amount, similar sleep) and note how you feel. Personal results are noisy, but it's better than paying double on faith.

## Safety: Who Should Be Careful With Each

Both products are generally well tolerated in healthy adults, but there are a few groups who should check with a doctor first.

**ZBiotics**
- People with a weakened immune system (for example, during chemotherapy or after an organ transplant) should ask a doctor before taking any live probiotic.
- If you're pregnant or breastfeeding, ask your doctor first.
- It's a genetically engineered organism. That's a personal preference question more than a safety one, but some people want to know.

**Cheers Restore and other DHM products**
- DHM may interact with some medicines, and human safety data at higher doses are limited. If you take prescription drugs, read our [DHM medication interactions guide](/never-hungover/dhm-medication-interactions-safety-guide-2025) and ask your pharmacist.
- If you have liver disease, talk to your doctor before taking any liver-targeted supplement.
- If you're pregnant or breastfeeding, skip it unless your doctor says otherwise.

**For both:** neither product changes your blood alcohol in a way that makes driving safe, and neither protects you from alcohol poisoning or long-term liver damage from heavy drinking. If you find yourself needing a hangover product most weekends, that's worth an honest conversation with a doctor about drinking.

## Who Should Pick Which

**Choose ZBiotics if:**
- You like the idea of one small drink before going out and nothing else to remember
- You don't want to swallow capsules
- The gut-acetaldehyde idea makes sense to you and you're fine with company-backed evidence
- Cost isn't a big concern

**Choose Cheers Restore if:**
- You'd rather take a pill than a drink
- You want the ingredient (DHM) with more independent research behind it
- You like an all-in-one formula with supporting ingredients and don't mind paying for the brand
- You want more flexibility on timing

**Choose plain DHM instead of either if:**
- You want the main active ingredient in Cheers without the brand premium
- You want to control the dose yourself
- You go out often enough that per-night cost adds up

If you're also weighing DHM against ZBiotics more generally, our [DHM vs ZBiotics comparison](/never-hungover/dhm-vs-zbiotics) goes deeper on that matchup, and our [Double Wood vs Cheers Restore](/never-hungover/double-wood-vs-cheers-restore-dhm-comparison-2025) and [Flyby vs Cheers](/never-hungover/flyby-vs-cheers-complete-comparison-2025) comparisons look at how Cheers stacks up against other DHM brands.

## The Verdict

**For evidence:** Cheers wins narrowly, because DHM has more independent research than ZBiotics' engineered probiotic. Neither has strong human trial evidence.

**For convenience:** ZBiotics, if you remember to drink it before your first drink. One bottle, done.

**For price:** neither. ZBiotics is the most expensive per night by far, and Cheers costs several times more than plain DHM with a similar main ingredient.

**For most people:** if you want to try a product at all, a well-dosed DHM supplement gives you the better-researched ingredient at the lowest cost. Cheers is a reasonable choice if you like its formula and brand. ZBiotics is worth trying if the drink format appeals to you and the price doesn't bother you, but go in knowing the evidence is mostly the company's own.

## The DHM Option: Same Main Ingredient as Cheers, Lower Price

If the comparison above points you toward DHM, here's where to start. These are affiliate links, which means we may earn a commission if you buy, at no extra cost to you.

- [No Days Wasted DHM Detox](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20) is our top-rated pick. It pairs 1,000 mg of DHM with L-cysteine, milk thistle, and electrolytes, similar in spirit to Cheers' all-in-one approach, at about $1.93 per serving at the price we last tracked.
- [Double Wood DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20) is the value pick: 1,000 mg of pure DHM at about $0.80 per serving.

Our [DHM dosage guide](/never-hungover/dhm-dosage-guide-2025) explains how much to take and when, the [dosage calculator](/dhm-dosage-calculator) personalizes it to your body weight and plans, and our [full DHM reviews](/reviews) compare every major brand, including Cheers, on dose, purity, and price. You can also line products up side by side on our [comparison page](/compare).

Whatever you choose, the same rule applies: these products are aimed at making a reasonable night a bit easier, not at making a heavy night consequence-free.

## The Bottom Line

- **ZBiotics** is an engineered probiotic drink that breaks down acetaldehyde in the gut. Clever idea, plausible mechanism, mostly company-backed evidence, and the highest cost per night.
- **Cheers Restore** is a DHM-based capsule with supporting ingredients. DHM has more independent research, mostly in animals, with limited human data.
- **Both are premium-priced.** Plain DHM supplements give you Cheers' main ingredient for much less.
- **Timing differs.** ZBiotics must go in before your first drink; DHM products are more flexible.
- **Neither one replaces** eating, pacing, water, and drinking less, and neither makes driving after drinking safe.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is ZBiotics or Cheers better for hangovers?**

Neither has strong independent human evidence, so there's no clear winner on results. Cheers is built around DHM, which has more published research (mostly in animals). ZBiotics uses an engineered probiotic with a plausible mechanism but mostly company-backed data. Cheers is also much cheaper per night. For many people, plain DHM is the best value of all.

**How does ZBiotics work?**

ZBiotics contains a *Bacillus subtilis* probiotic engineered to produce aldehyde dehydrogenase, the enzyme that breaks down acetaldehyde, a toxic by-product of alcohol. The idea is that it breaks down some acetaldehyde made in your gut. You drink it before your first alcoholic drink. It doesn't lower blood alcohol or make you less drunk.

**What is in Cheers Restore?**

Cheers Restore is built around DHM (dihydromyricetin), a compound from the Japanese raisin tree, along with supporting ingredients. Versions have included things like L-cysteine, milk thistle, and B vitamins. Check the current label for exact amounts, since formulas change.

**Can you take ZBiotics and Cheers together?**

There's no known conflict, since they work in different parts of the body. But the combination hasn't been studied, so there's no evidence it works better than either alone, and it doubles the cost. If you take prescription medicine, ask a pharmacist first.

**How much does ZBiotics cost per night compared to Cheers?**

At the prices we've seen, ZBiotics runs roughly $10 to $15 per night (one bottle), depending on pack size and subscription. Cheers Restore is about $3 per serving at the price we last tracked, with heavier nights sometimes calling for more. Plain DHM supplements can cost under $1 per serving.

**Does ZBiotics or Cheers lower your blood alcohol?**

No. Neither product is meant to lower blood alcohol or sober you up, and neither makes it safe to drive. ZBiotics says this directly about its own product. DHM's effects in animal studies don't translate into a safe way to drink more or drive.

**Is there a cheaper alternative to Cheers Restore?**

Yes. Cheers' main active ingredient is DHM, which is sold on its own by several brands. Pure DHM products often cost under $1 per serving. Our [DHM reviews](/reviews) compare the main options on dose, purity, and price.
